- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon) — adjust downward bias for short-term outlooks.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ to 65–68) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum — apply smoothing or decay factor to recent highs.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — increase sensitivity to last 7–10 days of history.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate volatility — cap forecast variance or use rolling median for stability.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5 days are above 70, don’t assume continuation; use 30-day moving average as anchor.
